sourceCitation: PRONI Certified Copy: Kilconriola Parish Marriage Register, William Moore and Isabella Law, March 29, 1846, Kirkinriola/Kilconriola Parish, Ballymena, County Antrim.
whatItProves: Marriage of William Moore (painter, Springwell Street) and Isabella Law (daughter of Patrick Law, brassfounder, Bridge Street), with addresses and occupations.
notes: Certified copy from Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI). Primary source for the Moore-Law family connection.

sourceCitation: Delaware Marriage Records, 1744, for Josiah Ramsey and Alice Bower (or possibly Elizabeth Hollis/Grigsby - needs verification).
whatItProves: Marriage of Josiah Ramsey Sr. in Delaware, establishing the early Ramsey family line. Exact spouse name needs verification.
notes: RESEARCH PRIORITY: Verify the exact name of Josiah Sr.'s wife from the original marriage record. Some sources suggest Alice Bower, others suggest Elizabeth Hollis or Elizabeth Grigsby.

sourceCitation: North Carolina Revolutionary War Pay Voucher for Josiah Ramsey, 1782, North Carolina Militia service.
whatItProves: Revolutionary War service of Josiah Ramsey Sr. in the North Carolina Militia, confirming his status as a patriot ancestor.
notes: Key document for SAR/DAR eligibility. Establishes Josiah Ramsey Sr. as a confirmed Revolutionary War veteran.

sourceCitation: State of Tennessee grant to Josiah Ramsey and his heirs, Claiborne County, entry no. 371, dated 22 April 1827 and surveyed 21 May 1827, for land on the waters of Mulberry Creek.
whatItProves: Josiah Ramsey held land in Claiborne County, Tennessee, on or near Mulberry Creek. The grant places his improvement there before his 1834 death and strengthens the Tennessee identity trail for the working Josiah profile.
notes: Primary source identity anchor. Keep with the Claiborne County Tennessee evidence set and use alongside the family memorial and residence trail.

sourceCitation: Tennessee, County Marriages, 1790-1950, Hancock County, Tennessee - Thomas Ramsey and Anna Hopkins marriage record.
whatItProves: Marriage of Thomas Ramsey (1799-1872) and Anna Hopkins (1807-1883) in Hancock County, Tennessee.
notes: RESEARCH PRIORITY: Locate and verify this marriage record in Tennessee county archives.

sourceCitation: U.S., War of 1812 Service Records, 1812-1815. Name: Josiah Ramsey. Company: 14 REG'T (MITCHISSON'S) Kentucky Militia. Rank at induction: Lieutenant. Rank at discharge: Adjutant. Roll Box 170. Microfilm Publication M602.
whatItProves: Josiah Ramsey served in the 14th Kentucky Militia during the War of 1812. The service record names him at induction as Lieutenant and at discharge as Adjutant.
notes: Primary source military record. Keep this service trail separate from the Revolutionary Josiah line until the identity bridge is explicit.

sourceCitation: 1840 U.S. Federal Census, Claiborne County, Tennessee - Elizabeth Ramsey household.
whatItProves: Elizabeth Ramsey as head of household in Claiborne County, Tennessee, with children aged 1787-1813 birth years. Helps identify the children of Josiah Ramsey Jr. and Elizabeth Cowan.
notes: RESEARCH PRIORITY: Examine the census image to identify all children in the household and match to the known Ramsey line.

sourceCitation: 1880 U.S. Federal Census, Richland Township, Decatur County, Iowa - Anna Ramsey household.
whatItProves: Anna Ramsey (1807-1883) appears as a widow in Richland Township, Decatur County, Iowa, confirming her residence after Thomas Ramsey's death.
notes: Supports the Ramsey family presence in Decatur County, Iowa.

sourceCitation: Southern Campaign American Revolution Pension Statements & Rosters, Pension Application of Charles Dyer R3176, transcribed and annotated by C. Leon Harris.
whatItProves: Charles Dyer’s discharge at Fort Randolph on September 25, 1778; his service in Captain William McKee’s company of the 12th Virginia Regiment; and the later county affidavit identifying his heirs and confirming the identity of the Revolutionary War pension applicant.
notes: Primary source transcript and scan for the discharge record. Later affidavit material in the same transcript names Jonathan Dyer among the heirs and ties the certificate back to Charles Dyer.

sourceCitation: Fold3 image 115273007, US Civil War Service Records, George W. Dyer, First Oregon Infantry, compiled from NARA carded records.
whatItProves: Service with the First Oregon Infantry in 1864.
notes: Metadata only for now. Original record image stays private.

whatItProves: Family memorial plaque names Josiah Ramsey and Elizabeth Cowan and lists their children, including Thomas Ramsey.
notes: Memorial record supports the family group and burial memory. It is not a civil birth record.

notes: Use this as supporting memorial evidence. The inscription and FamilySearch profile disagree on Josiah's birth year.

notes: Supporting primary record for the Revolutionary-era Josiah Ramsey profile. The image is a private screenshot of the FamilySearch record view.
